commit_message:
[Merged] Bug 1928666 part 4 - Support nursery-allocated buffer for Map/Set objects. r=jonco

This changes how the buffer is allocated/freed to be more similar to other objects with
nursery-allocated buffers. The finalizer is no longer called for nursery `Map`/`Set`
objects but we rely on the nursery's malloc buffer handling instead.

Nursery-allocating this buffer is a large speedup. We just have to fix up the hash table
chains after moving the buffer in memory.

Differential Revision: https://phabricator.services.mozilla.com/D228981

fix_commit_message:
Bug 1970095 - Clean up some Map/Set code. r=iain

Differential Revision: https://phabricator.services.mozilla.com/D252581
agent_reasoning: Merged diff composed mechanically by cherry-picking fix d578778fe18e on top of intro aa2d6702bbe1 via git's 3-way merge. Vulnerability (IntegerOverflow): The allocateCellBuffer function accepts a size_t numBytes parameter but passes it directly to AllocateCellBuffer<uint8_t>() which expects a uint32_t count parameter. When allocating buffers for very large Map/Set objects, the size can exceed UINT32_MAX (4GB), causing the value to be truncated to a much smaller 32-bit value. This results in allocating a significantly undersized buffer. Subsequently, when the Map/Set is rehashed (during OrderedHashTableImpl::rehash), memcpy operations copy data based on the expected larger size, but write to the smaller allocated buffer, causing a heap buffer overflow. Root cause: Type mismatch between the size_t used in OrderedHashTableObject.allocateCellBuffer() and the uint32_t expected by the GC's AllocateCellBuffer<T>() template function. The GC allocation functions were designed with the assumption that object buffers would never exceed 4GB, but no validation was added when the Map/Set code started using these functions for nursery-allocated buffers.
